factual_methodology.summary: Checked 16 Oct 2026 Fed G.17 output/utilization, IMF 13 Oct WEO outlook, Eurostat 15 Oct August factory data, IBGE 2 Oct August factory data, and BEA 30 Sep household figures. Explicitly distinguishes August from September and nominal from real measures.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: US specialized industrial expansion compared with weaker euro-area and Brazil factory readings; evaluates industry diffusion, physical capacity, financing, incomes and energy without copying the 18 Oct sovereign-debt report.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Two equivalent quantitative charts, two evidence tables, a causal flow and qualitative geographic map in both locales; chart values match.

research_depth.summary: US sector-level output and utilization juxtaposed with euro-area and Brazil August production and US household expenditure; documents limits of aggregation, transmission channels and falsifiers.

evidence_traceability.summary: Eight identical source URLs in English and Portuguese across Federal Reserve, IMF, EIA, ICI, Treasury, Eurostat, IBGE and BEA; primary observations dated and source vintages distinguished.

counterfactual_review.summary: Alternative explanations include energy-driven utility demand, inventory timing, narrow semiconductors, geographically segmented cycles and future spread to capital goods and wages.

contrary_evidence: A national utilization gap cannot determine whether a local power network or semiconductor fabrication line has spare capacity.
Rising nominal household spending does not imply real purchasing-power gains.
Euro area and Brazil August output data are not contemporaneous with US September industrial figures; cross-country comparisons do not establish a shared causal shock.
limitations: September Fed industrial observations are preliminary and scheduled for benchmark revisions.
Sectoral factory data cannot identify ownership or beneficiary geography of capital returns.
This internal QA checks key institutional anchors and article comparability, not external peer review of all interpretation.
notes: Internal substantive bilingual editorial QA; 8 same institutional URL references and aligned source date units checked; latest material created after correction of research depth constraints. Final review of the factual-neutral macro opening self-reference edit; citation and quantitative series unchanged.

en.title: Global Macro — US industrial output rebounds while manufacturing capacity remains underused
en.deck: September output rose 0.7% but utilities and semiconductors outpaced ordinary manufacturing, while overall utilization remained below normal.
en.regime: Selective US industrial recovery, uneven capacity use, and high international energy costs.
en.key_risk: Specialized investment fails to broaden because of local infrastructure, financing and energy constraints.
